stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Describes a complex cross-functional feature spanning GO, UP, and MX (live preview). Needs full elaboration via openspec to define AC and technical depth, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge cases. No prior hand-curation detected.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Contentstack Live Preview integration. The codebase already has live_preview config in src/services/contentstack.ts (enable flag, management_token, host) but real-time content updates without page reload require wiring the Live Preview SDK into the content delivery pipeline. Attachment points: Stack initialization, useContent hook (236+ consumers), and ContentstackContext provider. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs stop at our boundary: what our code sends, receives, and renders given mocked Contentstack responses.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria but valuable architectural notes identifying attachment points (Stack init, useContent hook, ContentstackContext) and the boundary constraint that VCs stop at our code boundary with mocked Contentstack. I built the full AC set from the story title, description, and those notes. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could not read the four files listed in technicalNotes (contentstack.ts, useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, ContentstackLink.tsx). My ACs are based on standard Contentstack Live Preview integration patterns and the config fields mentioned in openspec's notes (enable, management_token, host). If these files contain existing partial implementations or non-standard patterns, some ACs may need adjustment. AC-9 (security) may need revision depending on whether this is a client-side or server-side rendered app — Contentstack's live preview SDK typically runs client-side with the management_token, which is a known security consideration. AC-15 (bundle exclusion) assumes tree-shaking is feasible; this may need softening if the SDK doesn't support it.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: The spec pipeline failed to produce its primary artifact — the acceptanceCriteria array remains empty despite both agents claiming to have processed the story. OpenSpec provided valuable architectural notes (attachment points: Stack init, useContent hook, ContentstackContext; boundary constraint around mocked Contentstack) but did not elaborate any ACs (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). Speckit claims it 'built the full AC set' yet acceptanceChanged is also false and no ACs are present in the story data; this is a contradiction that indicates either a write failure or the ACs were never actually persisted. Additionally, Speckit self-disclosed that it could not read the four key source files (contentstack.ts, useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, ContentstackLink.tsx), meaning any ACs it did generate would be based on standard patterns rather than the actual codebase. Both agents added non-overlapping value at the notes level (OpenSpec: architecture and integration points; Speckit: gap analysis and security caveats), but the core deliverable — testable, persisted acceptance criteria — is missing. No story splits were produced despite this being a complex cross-functional feature spanning GO, UP, and MX teams, which likely warrants decomposition. Speckit's self-flagged caveats on AC-9 (security model for management_token) and AC-15 (bundle exclusion feasibility) further underscore that the spec is not implementation-ready. Human review is required to either re-run the pipeline with source file access or hand-curate the ACs.
